Name: Nimzo-Larsen Attack
Eco: A01
Moves: 1. b3
Style Tags: positional, solid, tricky
Difficulty: beginner
Plays As: White
Key Ideas: White aims to fianchetto the queen’s bishop and exert pressure on the centre from the side, while keeping the pawn structure flexible.
Description: The Nimzo‑Larsen Attack is a flexible, hypermodern opening that lets White develop the queen’s bishop to b2 and challenge Black’s central pawns from a distance. It suits players who like to control the centre indirectly and are comfortable with unbalanced pawn structures. Typical plans include pressuring the d5‑square, preparing e4 or c4, and using the bishop’s long diagonal to create threats. Common mistakes are moving the b‑pawn again too early or neglecting development, which can give Black a strong centre.

Name: Bird Opening
Eco: A02
Moves: 1. f4
Style Tags: aggressive, tactical
Difficulty: intermediate
Plays As: White
Key Ideas: White seeks early control of the e5‑square and opens the f‑file to launch a kingside attack while challenging Black’s central presence.
Description: The Bird Opening is a flank opening that aims for an aggressive, attacking game. It suits players who like to fight for the initiative early and are comfortable with unbalanced positions. Typical plans involve pushing e4, developing the bishop to g2, and using the f‑file for pressure, while keeping an eye on the weak king’s side squares. Common mistakes are neglecting central development and allowing Black to seize the centre with …d5 and …e5.

Name: Zukertort Opening
Eco: A04
Moves: 1. Nf3
Style Tags: solid, positional
Difficulty: beginner
Plays As: White
Key Ideas: Develop the knight to a natural square, control the centre indirectly and keep options open for flexible piece placement.
Description: The Zukertort Opening lets White develop calmly without committing central pawns early, making it a good choice for players who prefer a solid, flexible style. It suits beginners who want to learn piece development and transposition ideas. Typical plans involve a later c4 or d4 push, fianchettoing the bishop, and castling early. Common mistakes are grabbing space too early with pawn moves that block pieces or neglecting king safety.

Name: King's Indian Attack
Eco: A07
Moves: 1. Nf3 d5 2. g3
Style Tags: solid, positional
Difficulty: beginner
Plays As: White
Key Ideas: White builds a flexible setup, fianchettoes the king's bishop, and prepares a pawn advance on the kingside to launch an attack while keeping the center under control with pieces.
Description: The King's Indian Attack is a quiet, system‑based opening that lets White develop quickly without memorising many theory lines. It suits players who like steady piece play and a later kingside assault, especially against Black’s solid pawn structures. Typical plans involve a fianchettoed bishop, a knight on f3, and a pawn storm with f‑ and g‑pawns to open lines toward the black king. Common mistakes are moving the same piece repeatedly, neglecting central counterplay, and launching the attack before the pieces are coordinated.

Name: Réti Opening
Eco: A09
Moves: 1. Nf3 d5 2. c4
Style Tags: solid, positional
Difficulty: intermediate
Plays As: White
Key Ideas: White aims to control the centre from the flanks, keeping the pawn structure flexible and preparing a later central break while developing pieces harmoniously.
Description: The Réti is a flexible, hypermodern opening that lets White develop quietly and challenge Black’s centre from the side. It suits players who prefer a solid, strategic game and are comfortable with transpositions into various structures. Typical plans include fianchettoing the king’s bishop, playing c4‑c5 or d4 at the right moment, and using the knights to exert pressure. Common mistakes are grabbing space too early, neglecting development, or allowing Black to seize the centre unchallenged.

Name: English Opening
Eco: A10
Moves: 1. c4
Style Tags: positional, solid
Difficulty: beginner
Plays As: White
Key Ideas: White aims to control the centre from the flanks, using the c‑pawn to influence d5 and keep a flexible pawn structure.
Description: The English Opening lets you develop pieces behind a solid pawn chain and avoid early direct confrontations. It suits players who prefer a slow buildup, focusing on piece placement and long‑term pressure rather than sharp tactics. Typical plans include expanding on the queenside, exchanging central pawns to free the bishops, and later striking in the centre or kingside when the position is ready. Common mistakes are moving the same piece repeatedly, neglecting development, and trying to force premature attacks before the position is coordinated.

Name: Englund Gambit
Eco: A40
Moves: 1. d4 e5
Style Tags: aggressive, tactical, tricky
Difficulty: intermediate
Plays As: Black
Key Ideas: Black sacrifices a pawn early to gain rapid development and seize the initiative against White's center.
Description: The Englund Gambit is a sharp, surprise weapon that leads to unbalanced, tactical play. It suits players who enjoy active piece play and are comfortable with taking risks. Black aims for quick development, pressure on White's d‑pawn and open lines, often targeting the king before White can consolidate. A common mistake is trying to hold onto the pawn or ignoring Black's initiative, which can leave Black with a losing position.

Name: English Defense
Eco: A40
Moves: 1. d4 b6
Style Tags: solid, defensive, counterattacking
Difficulty: intermediate
Plays As: Black
Key Ideas: Black fianchettoes the queen's bishop and challenges White's centre from a distance, aiming to undermine d4 and c4 squares.
Description: The English Defense is a flexible, hyper‑modern system that suits players who like to let White occupy the centre first and then strike back. Black develops the bishop to b7, prepares …e6 and …Bb7, and looks for breaks with …c5 or …e5 to undermine White's pawn chain. It works well for players comfortable with a slower, maneuvering game and who can handle slightly cramped positions. Common mistakes include neglecting development of the kingside pieces and allowing White to consolidate the centre without counter‑play.

Name: Colle System
Eco: A40
Moves: 1. d4 g6 2. Nf3 Bg7 3. e3 c5 4. Bd3 Qa5+
Style Tags: solid, positional
Difficulty: beginner
Plays As: White
Key Ideas: White develops quickly and prepares a central e4 pawn break while keeping a solid pawn structure.
Description: The Colle System is a simple, system-based opening for White that emphasizes quick piece development and a later e4 push. It suits players who prefer clear, straightforward plans and want to avoid deep opening theory. Typical ideas include developing knights, placing the bishop on d3, castling early, and then preparing the central break with e4, often supported by c3 and Nbd2. Common mistakes are delaying the e4 advance, neglecting king safety, or launching premature attacks without proper piece coordination.

Name: Old Indian Defense
Eco: A41
Moves: 1. d4 d6 2. c4
Style Tags: solid, positional, counterattacking
Difficulty: intermediate
Plays As: Black
Key Ideas: Black seeks a flexible pawn structure, prepares a central pawn break and develops pieces behind a solid setup while keeping the king safe.
Description: The Old Indian is a quiet, solid opening for Black that avoids early theory. It suits players who like to build a strong pawn chain and wait for the right moment to strike in the center. Typical plans involve developing the knights to natural squares, placing the bishop on a safe diagonal, and castling early. Common mistakes are playing too passively and allowing White to seize space with aggressive pawn advances.

Name: Benoni Defense
Eco: A43
Moves: 1. d4 c5
Style Tags: aggressive, tactical, counterattacking
Difficulty: intermediate
Plays As: Black
Key Ideas: Black seeks to undermine White's central d4 pawn with timely pawn breaks and active piece play, exchanging space for dynamic counter‑chances.
Description: The Benoni is a sharp, unbalanced opening that suits players who enjoy active piece play and are comfortable with a cramped position. Black accepts less space in the centre in order to generate counter‑play on the queenside and through central pawn breaks. Typical plans involve rapid development, pressure on White's center, and creating threats before White can fully consolidate. Common mistakes are trying to hold the pawn chain too rigidly or neglecting development, which lets White solidify the spatial advantage.

Name: Trompowsky Attack
Eco: A45
Moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. Bg5
Style Tags: aggressive, tactical
Difficulty: intermediate
Plays As: White
Key Ideas: White develops the bishop early to put pressure on Black's knight and create threats before Black can complete normal development.
Description: The opening gives White an active piece early and suits players who like to seize the initiative. It works well against players who prefer solid, slow setups because the bishop can quickly become a nuisance. Typical plans involve exchanging the bishop for the knight, then playing c4 or e4 to open the centre. A common mistake is delaying development of the other pieces, allowing Black to equalise easily.

Name: Torre Attack
Eco: A48
Moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. Nf3 g6 3. Bg5
Style Tags: solid, positional
Difficulty: beginner
Plays As: White
Key Ideas: White develops the bishop to g5 early to put pressure on Black's knight and control the e5 square while keeping a flexible pawn structure.
Description: The Torre Attack is a quiet system that lets White avoid heavy theory and play a simple plan. It suits players who prefer steady development and want to limit Black's counter‑play. Typical ideas are to castle quickly, play c3 and e4 to claim the centre, and use the bishop on g5 to exchange the key defender. Common mistakes are moving the bishop multiple times or trying to force an early attack before the centre is secure.

Name: London System
Eco: A48
Moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. Nf3 g6 3. Bf4
Style Tags: solid, positional
Difficulty: beginner
Plays As: White
Key Ideas: White aims for a solid, flexible setup with the queen's bishop on its natural square, a strong pawn chain centered on d‑pawn supported by the e‑pawn, and quick development of the knights, keeping the centre under control while preparing a safe king.
Description: The London System is a quiet, solid opening that lets White develop without memorising long theory. It suits players who prefer a safe, strategic game and like to build a strong pawn centre before launching attacks. Typical plans involve developing the queen’s bishop to its natural square, supporting the d‑pawn with the e‑pawn, and later deciding whether to expand in the centre or launch a kingside attack. Common mistakes are moving the bishop too early, neglecting king safety, or trying to force premature pawn breaks.

Name: Benko Gambit
Eco: A57
Moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 c5 3. d5 b5
Style Tags: aggressive, tactical, counterattacking
Difficulty: intermediate
Plays As: Black
Key Ideas: Black sacrifices a pawn to gain long‑term pressure on the queenside and control of the a‑ and b‑files.
Description: The Benko Gambit is a dynamic opening that suits players who like active piece play and long‑term pressure rather than immediate material grabs. Black gives up a pawn early to obtain strong control of the a‑ and b‑files and to create lasting threats against White’s queenside. Typical plans involve placing rooks on the open files, pressuring the c‑ and a‑pawns, and using the bishop on the long diagonal. Common mistakes are trying to hold onto the pawn too long or ignoring Black’s piece activity, which lets Black’s initiative grow.

Name: Dutch Defense
Eco: A80
Moves: 1. d4 f5
Style Tags: aggressive, counterattacking, solid
Difficulty: intermediate
Plays As: Black
Key Ideas: Black seeks to control the e4 square and generate a kingside attack while keeping a flexible pawn structure.
Description: The Dutch Defense is an aggressive opening where Black immediately challenges White's centre with ...f5, creating unbalanced positions. It suits players who enjoy active piece play and attacking chances on the kingside, but it demands careful handling of the weakened dark‑squared diagonal. Typical plans include advancing the g‑ and e‑pawns, developing the bishop to g7 or e7, and using the f‑pawn to support a kingside assault. Common mistakes are neglecting king safety, overextending the pawn chain, and allowing White to dominate the centre with e4.

Name: Pirc Defense
Eco: B00
Moves: 1. e4 d6
Style Tags: solid, counterattacking
Difficulty: intermediate
Plays As: Black
Key Ideas: Black lets White build a strong pawn centre and then undermines it with timely pawn breaks and piece pressure.
Description: The Pirc is a flexible, hypermodern opening where Black invites White to claim the centre with pawns and then attacks it from the flanks. It suits players who like solid structures and counter‑attacking chances rather than early tactical fireworks. Typical plans involve developing the kingside fianchetto, striking with ...c5 or ...e5, and using the central pawn tension to create activity. Common mistakes are grabbing space too early with ...e5 or neglecting development, which can leave Black cramped.

Description: The Nimzowitsch Defense is a hypermodern opening that invites White to occupy the centre and then attacks it from the flanks. It suits players who like unbalanced positions and are comfortable with counter‑play rather than early pawn grabs. Typical plans include striking with ...d5 or ...e5, developing the bishop to g4 or f5, and using the knights to pressure the centre. Common mistakes are grabbing space too early with ...e5 or ...d5 without preparation, which can leave Black behind in development.

Eco: B01

Style Tags: solid, counterattacking
Difficulty: beginner
Plays As: Black
Key Ideas: Black immediately contests White's central pawn, often exchanging on e4 to gain active piece play and a clear development plan.
Description: The Scandinavian is a direct, straightforward opening that suits players who like to challenge the centre from move one. Black aims to trade the d‑pawn for White's e‑pawn and then develop the queen and knights quickly. Typical plans involve rapid piece activity and pressure on the e‑file while keeping the pawn structure simple. Common mistakes are moving the queen too many times early and neglecting king safety.

Key Ideas: Black invites White to occupy the centre with pawns and then attacks the overextended centre.
Description: The Alekhine Defense is a provocative opening that lets White claim space early while Black prepares to undermine that centre later. It suits players who enjoy dynamic, counter‑attacking play and are comfortable letting the opponent overextend. Typical plans involve striking at the central pawn chain, developing pieces to active squares, and creating pressure on the centre. Common mistakes are grabbing material too quickly or allowing White’s centre to solidify without enough counter‑play.

Description: The Modern Defense is a flexible, hypermodern system that suits players who like to let the opponent build a pawn centre first. It works well for those comfortable with piece play and waiting for the right moment to strike back with ... or ... . Typical plans involve a kingside fianchetto, timely ...‑breaks, and exchanging the dark‑squared bishop for White's strong centre. Common mistakes are grabbing space too early with ... or neglecting king safety while the bishop remains on the long diagonal.

Difficulty: intermediate

Description: The Caro‑Kann gives Black a sturdy, less risky way to meet 1.e4, ideal for players who prefer a calm, strategic game rather than sharp tactics. It suits players who like to build a strong, flexible pawn chain and develop pieces harmoniously. Typical plans involve exchanging the d‑pawn for White’s e‑pawn, developing the bishop outside the pawn chain, and later striking in the center with ...c5 or ...f6. Common mistakes are playing too passively, neglecting development, or trying to force premature attacks before the position is ready.

Eco: B20

Style Tags: aggressive, tactical, counterattacking
Difficulty: intermediate
Plays As: Black
Key Ideas: Black challenges White's central pawn on e4 with the c‑pawn, creating asymmetrical pawn structures that give Black active counterplay, especially on the queenside and centre.
Description: The Sicilian Defense is a dynamic opening that seeks immediate counter‑chances rather than a symmetrical build‑up. It suits players who enjoy unbalanced positions and are comfortable generating active play on the queenside while contesting the centre. Typical plans include expanding with ... and targeting White's central and kingside weaknesses. Common mistakes are moving the same piece repeatedly, neglecting development, and allowing White to seize a strong central pawn majority.

Eco: C00

Style Tags: solid, positional, counterattacking
Difficulty: intermediate
Plays As: Black
Key Ideas: Black seeks to undermine White's central pawn on e4 by striking with the pawn on the second rank, creating a solid pawn chain and preparing counterplay on the queen's side.
Description: The French Defense gives Black a solid, sometimes slightly cramped position where the fight for the center is central. It suits players who enjoy strategic maneuvering and are comfortable with a blocked pawn structure. Typical plans involve challenging White's center, exchanging pieces to relieve cramped space, and launching a counter‑attack on the queen’s side. Common mistakes include trying to launch premature attacks before completing development and overlooking the weakness of the d5 square.

Style Tags: aggressive, tactical
Difficulty: intermediate
Plays As: White
Key Ideas: White immediately challenges Black's central pawn to open lines and accelerate development for a rapid attack.
Description: The Center Game is an open, aggressive opening that seeks early central tension and quick piece activity. It suits players who enjoy tactical opportunities and like to seize the initiative early. Typical plans involve rapid development, using the open centre to launch attacks on the king, especially targeting the f‑pawn and exploiting open files. Common mistakes include bringing the queen out too soon, neglecting king safety, and trying to hold onto the pawn at the cost of development.

Name: Danish Gambit
Eco: C21
Moves: 1. e4 e5 2. d4 exd4 3. c3
Style Tags: aggressive, tactical
Difficulty: intermediate
Plays As: White
Key Ideas: White sacrifices one or two central pawns to gain lead in development and open lines for a swift attack on Black's king.
Description: The Danish Gambit is a sharp, attacking opening that suits players who like to seize the initiative early. By giving up material, White aims to develop pieces quickly and create dangerous threats against Black's king. It works best against opponents who are uncomfortable defending under pressure, but the sacrifice can backfire if Black consolidates and returns material. Common mistakes include delaying development, trying to hold onto the extra pawn, or underestimating Black's counter‑play.

Difficulty: beginner

Description: The Bishop's Opening leads to open, attacking games and suits players who like to seize the initiative early. It works well for those who enjoy quick development and targeting the weak f7 point. Typical plans include castling quickly, bringing the queen and knights into the attack, and using the bishop’s diagonal to create threats. A common mistake is neglecting central pawn structure or over‑extending without enough support.

Difficulty: intermediate

Description: The Vienna Game lets White develop the knight to c3 early, giving flexibility to play a quiet d4 or an aggressive f4 pawn storm. It suits players who like to keep options open and are comfortable with both calm and sharp play. Typical plans include building a strong centre with d4 or launching a kingside attack with f4 and Nf3. Common mistakes are neglecting development of the bishop and over‑extending the pawn structure before completing piece coordination.

It works best for those who like quick piece development and direct threats against the opponent's king. Typical plans involve using the open lines to launch a swift assault, often with the bishop and queen targeting the vulnerable f7 square.
